articles.title: Structured light in hyperbolic metamaterials
articles.authors: Yuruo Zheng, Jiaren Tan, Hooman Barati Sedeh, Natalia M. Litchinitser
articles.summary: The synergy between structured light and hyperbolic metamaterials creates new opportunities for fundamental optical science and advanced photonic applications. We examine the emerging intersection of these two fields. We introduce the principal degrees of freedom of structured optical fields and summarize the distinctive hyperbolic dispersion, high wavevector modes, strong anisotropy, and enhanced light–matter interactions supported by multilayer, nanowire, and natural hyperbolic platforms. …

articles.title: Ultralow‐Loss, High‐Efficiency and Fast Thermo‐Optic Modulator Based on β'‐In 2 Se 3
articles.authors: Jialing Jian, Qingyan Deng, Jianghong Wu, Jiaxi Yang, Yuting Ye, Bo Tang, Xiang Xu, Keyu Qian, Jiaxin Zhang, Junying Li, Hui Ma, Chuyu Zhong, Zhengjin Weng, Yuanfang Yu, Shaoqing Xiao, Hongtao Lin, Haiyan Nan, Lan Li
institutions: School of Integrated Circuits Jiangnan University Wuxi China
Institute of Microelectronics Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
articles.summary: Thermo‐optic (TO) modulators based on conventional materials face an unavoidable trade‐off among optical loss, power consumption, and response time. Here, we overcome this trilemma using a β′‐In 2 Se 3 microheater whose high electrical conductivity, optical transparency and low refractive index simultaneously enable ultralow propagation loss and high TO efficiency in the telecommunication band. This van der Waals material offers a potential pathway toward CMOS back‐end‐of‐line‐compatible integration with microring resonators (MRRs) using an ultrathin optical isolation layer, thereby facilitating fast thermal conduction and efficient thermal modulation. …

articles.title: A graphene-based tunable metasurface for on-demand terahertz beam-number switching with joint amplitude-phase optimization
articles.authors: Xingyu Guo, Yan Teng, Chun Li, Zhengwei Huang, Haobo Chen, Jiangtao Luo, Ziteng Wang, Ling Jiang
institutions: College of Information Science and Technology
articles.summary: On-demand beam-number switching is important for reconfigurable terahertz (THz) wavefront manipulation because it directly controls scattering-channel allocation, spatial coverage, and power distribution. However, it requires selective suppression of designated beams, stable preservation of remaining main beams, and adaptation to discrete device states. Here, we propose an on-demand THz beam-number switching method based on a graphene-tunable metasurface. A joint amplitude-phase particle swarm optimization model is developed by combining prior-phase inheritance, constrained joint amplitude-phase optimization, and device-aware quantized amplitude optimization. …

articles.title: Label-free counting of nanoparticles in a perfused microphysiological system by digital holography
articles.authors: Tomoyoshi Inoue, Iroha Okuda, Yasuhiro Ishihara
articles.summary: A wide variety of nanoparticles exist in the atmosphere, and there are concerns regarding the impact of their inhalation on the respiratory system. Recently, the respiratory effects of fine particles have been investigated using microfluidic systems (e.g., microphysiological systems), such as “lung-on-a-chip” devices; however, these studies often lack direct observation of the nanoparticles themselves. This is due to the absence of technology capable of detecting unlabeled particles under flow conditions. We have developed a holographic system that detects and counts nanoparticles flowing through a microphysiological system without labeling. …

articles.title: Residual Errors Alter AI Chest-Radiograph Findings: Outage-Based Design of Free-Space Optical Links for Medical Image Delivery
articles.authors: Entidhar Mhawes Zghair, Seham Ahmed Hashem, Ali Mahdi Hammadi
articles.summary: Pathological chest radiographs are often assumed to be more vulnerable to channel impairments than normal ones. We simulated sending 250 NIH ChestX-ray14 radiographs from five diagnostic classes, in three payload formats sharing identical channel realizations, over a 1 km, 1550 nm free-space optical link with Gamma–Gamma fading, pointing errors and RS(255,204) coding. After an error event, diagnostic class explained 0.4–5% of the between-image variance in quality beyond grey-level statistics and JPEG size. A second, partially overlapping sample confirmed this, and a bit-level analysis explains why. …

articles.title: Binary Representation of Grayscale Images for DMD-Based Coherent Spatial Filtering Systems
articles.authors: Pavel A. Cheremkhin, Iuliia S. Lenkova, Daria V. Pavlenko, Vladislav G. Rodin, Anna V. Shifrina, Rostislav S. Starikov, Fedor A. Ushakov, Evgenii Yu. Zlokazov
institutions: Institute for Laser and Plasma Technologies
articles.summary: Fast optical data processing provides incredible opportunities for present-day and near-future tasks: pattern recognition, object tracking, beam shaping, development of diffractive neural networks, 3D-display and lithographic systems, etc. Digital micromirror devices (DMD) can display binary megapixel images with frame rates of tens of thousands Hz. However, grayscale images are more convenient for practical implementations. In this paper we analyzed several digital halftoning and binarization methods in search of the best one for a coherent DMD-based spatial filtering system. …

articles.title: Design of a compact, fast-switching high-voltage pulser for high-repetition-rate miniature time-of-flight mass spectrometers
articles.authors: Cao G, Huang Y, Zhu L, Zhou Z, Qi F
articles.summary: To meet the demand for miniaturized, low-power high-voltage pulse power supplies for time-of-flight mass spectrometers (TOF-MS), we designed a compact half-bridge push-pull pulse power supply. The power supply achieves a frequency range of 1-100 kHz, a maximum output voltage of 800 V, pulse-width adjustment in 0.1 μs steps, and a power consumption of ∼10 W. Electrical characterization shows that the rise time is less than 10 ns, overshoot is below 5%, amplitude and period stability are excellent, and the synchronization between positive and negative pulses is reliable. …
